patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — BigCommerce and OpenCart share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose BigCommerce only if your buying job matches “Open-SaaS ecommerce platform — Core $39/mo ($29 annual), Growth $105 ($79), Scale $399 ($2” rather than OpenCart's shape. Choose OpenCart only if your buying job matches “GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by” rather than BigCommerce's shape. Workflow advantage: BigCommerce leans catalog-management, wholesale-b2b; OpenCart leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — BigCommerce and OpenCart share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: BigCommerce is Open-SaaS ecommerce platform — Core $39/mo ($29 annual), Growth $105 ($79), Scale $399 ($299); GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees; OpenCart is GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by secondary sources (confirm live). WooCommerce kee.
- Company-size focus: BigCommerce (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs OpenCart (small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: BigCommerce-leaning catalog-management, wholesale-b2b vs OpenCart-leaning —.
- Researched limits: BigCommerce — 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription; OpenCart — Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0.

Limitations — BigCommerce: 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription; Native POS/retail depth trails Shopify/Square for omnichannel-first merchants; OpenCart: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0; Managed cloud floors are not first-party confirmed here — confirm live before budgeting.

Poor-fit cases: BigCommerce is a poor fit when that limitation bites: 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription · OpenCart is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0 · Avoid BigCommerce if you actually need OpenCart's motion (GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
